No, that is not correct. In Switzerland, voting rights in federal elections are generally restricted to Swiss citizens. Foreign residents, regardless of the type of residence permit they hold (such as a C permit, which is typically for long-term residence), do not have the right to vote at the federal level.

However, some cantons and municipalities may grant voting rights to foreign residents under specific conditions, such as long-term residency or integration requirements, but this varies by location and is not a federal right.
